developer: Konza Technopolis Development Authority (KoTDA); Huawei Cloud Stack technology partner

Huawei Cloud Stack deployed a Tier-III standards data center. Same canonical project recorded under Kajiado/Makueni with boundary caveat (Konza planning zone spans Machakos/Makueni/Kajiado). developer: Konza Technopolis Development Authority (KoTDA); PPP investor to be selected
notes: PPP Directorate approved the Konza Data Centre Cloud and Smart City Facilities expansion to feasibility stage (Jan 2026); Construction Review Online (May 2026) reports Sh5 billion set aside for a new data center at Konza with cloud infrastructure upgrades and digital services expansion. Same canonical project recorded under Kajiado (cross-county Konza footprint). No public MW capacity found.

name: Cloudoon Masinga 101 (MAS101) green data centre
notes: Cloudoon MAS101 announced 2022: 10-acre campus near the Seven Forks/Masinga hydro dams (Masinga, Machakos County per ColoMap), claimed Kenya's largest data centre with 10MW+ IT load, 200,000 sq ft raised floor, 2,500+ racks, hydro-powered liquid-cooled green design. Current construction/operational status unverified; grade B for announcement, current status U.

name: Konza National Data Centre (boundary record)
developer: Konza Technopolis Development Authority (KoTDA); Huawei Cloud Stack technology partner
notes: Included for Makueni coverage: Konza Technopolis and its National Data Centre are publicly described as spanning the Machakos/Makueni/Kajiado buffer/planning zone (Wikipedia; Konza materials reference benefits to Makueni). The facility itself is confirmed operational (Tier III, KoTDA), but parcel-level county attribution is unresolved; same canonical record under Machakos and Kajiado.

name: iColo Mombasa One (MBA1) Miritini
notes: Official iColo page: MBA1 at Miritini operational since 2017; Miritini campus to expand to 3 data centres, 18,000 sqm, 13 MW total IT load and 1,800 racks. iColo homepage lists Mombasa One IT power 0.9 MW. KIXP interconnects MBA1 and MBA2; Mombasa is the main subsea-cable landing point.

name: iColo Mombasa Two (MBA2) Nyali
notes: iColo announced MBA2 in Nyali (2021) with ~1.6 MW design capacity; DCD reported completion with 1.7 MW capacity, ~1,200 sqm and roughly 580-600 racks, greenfield site near cable landing points. KIXP interconnects MBA1/MBA2. Facility status operational.

name: iXAfrica Nairobi Campus NBOX1
notes: iXAfrica NBOX1 at Cabanas/Mombasa Road, Nairobi: first phase (4.5 MW, 780 racks) launched March 2025; overall design capacity 22.5 MW, Tier III-standard carrier-neutral, AI-ready hyperscale campus (East Africa's largest); KIXP peering PoP on site; host facility for the announced Oracle OCI Kenya region. 22.5 MW is campus design capacity, not current IT load.

name: iXAfrica NBOX1.2 (Nairobi campus expansion)
notes: iXAfrica is developing NBOX1.2 with designed IT capacity of 18 MW as the next phase of the Nairobi campus (Developing Telecoms); part of the same campus as NBOX1. Status planned/under development; no separate construction evidence found.

name: Africa Data Centres Nairobi NBO1 (Sameer / East Africa Data Centre)
notes: Africa Data Centres NBO1 at Sameer Industrial Park, Mombasa Road: 2,000 sqm secured space, 7.5 MW available site capacity (official page), 4 Uptime Institute Tier III-certified data halls; Tier III certification renewed (official news); first East Africa DC with Uptime Tier III and PCI DSS.

name: Africa Data Centres second Nairobi facility
notes: ADC announced (Nov 2021) development of a second Nairobi data centre of up to 20 MW IT load and was securing land for a third facility. Later public status not confirmed in accessible sources; treat as planned with status U for current progress.

name: Africa Data Centres Sameer facility expansion
notes: Cassava/Africa Data Centres announced expansion of the Sameer (NBO1) facility in Nairobi by up to 15 MW of IT load using modular design (Dec 2022). Current progress unverified.

name: Digital Realty / iColo Nairobi One (NBO1) Karen
notes: Official iColo page: NBO1 launched September 2019 in Karen with 280 racks and 624 sqm customer space; DCD reported design support up to 825 kW IT load (0.825 MW). Operational.

name: Digital Realty / iColo Nairobi Two (NBO2) Langata

name: PAIX Nairobi-1 (NBO1) Britam Tower
notes: PAIX Nairobi-1 at Britam Tower, Upper Hill: 240 cabinets, ~1.5 MVA total power, opened November 2020; official PAIX page describes NBO-1 as Nairobi's best-connected DC with access to KIXP, Nairobi-IX and major carriers; LINX Nairobi expanded its fabric to PAIX NBO-1.

name: Telkom Kenya Data Centre (Upper Hill)
notes: Telkom Kenya launched a Ksh150 million data centre in Nairobi's Upper Hill (July 2018): phase one ~1,460 sq ft of rack space for colocation/hosting, served by 3 diverse fibre routes (Westlands, GPO, South-Hill exchanges). Operational; market report (2024) lists Telkom Kenya among key Kenya DC investors. No public MW capacity found.

name: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) Kenya public cloud region (hosted at iXAfrica)
notes: iXAfrica announced 2026-01-27 it will host Oracle's first public cloud region in Kenya at its NBOX1 Nairobi facility (first OCI region in East & Central Africa, ~50kW AI-ready density; first mooted by President Ruto Jan 2024). Cloud region != facility; recorded as cloud/project seed - service launch must be confirmed on Oracle's official region list (per KE methodology). No standalone facility beyond iXAfrica NBOX1.

name: Safaricom Nairobi Data Centre
notes: Safaricom official wholesale page states its data centres are located in Thika, Nairobi and Kisumu; a Nairobi metro facility exists as part of that portfolio (specific address/capacity not published on the official page). No public MW capacity found.

name: EcoCloud Olkaria Project Eagle (KenGen Green Energy Park)
developer: EcoCloud Data Centre; KenGen Green Energy Park host (with KenGen, Konza Technopolis, G42 collaboration)
notes: EcoCloud broke ground on Project Eagle at KenGen Green Energy Park, Olkaria (Nakuru County) in Sept 2023: phase one 24 MW IT capacity across eight 3MW data halls (300-500 racks each), expected total consumption ~70 MW, geothermal power from KenGen; $600M project coverage Sep 2025. NOTE: 2026 reporting (Ghanamma 2026-07-17) describes the site as largely empty with the broader Microsoft/G42 1GW ambition stalled - treat construction progress as uncertain (B for ground-breaking; current status U).

name: Microsoft/G42 Olkaria geothermal data centre campus (East Africa Azure cloud region)
developer: G42 with Microsoft and Kenyan partners (KenGen/EcoCloud)
notes: Microsoft/G42 announced (2024-05-22) a $1B digital ecosystem initiative including a geothermal-powered Olkaria data-centre campus for a new East Africa Azure cloud region (initial ~100MW, G42/EcoCloud collaboration with potential expansion to 1GW). 2026 reporting: project stalled/paused over national grid capacity and payment guarantees (Reuters 2026-05-10, DCD), with the Olkaria site reported largely empty (July 2026). Azure region list does not yet include Kenya. Status planned/uncertain - announcement grade A, current status B/C.
